page: The Vultr voc-s-4c-32gb-960s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance built on the x86_64 AMD EPYC architecture. It provides 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core, running at a base clock of 2.0 GHz. The processor includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, alongside instruction support for AVX, AVX-512 (including VNNI and BF16), and cryptographic acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA-NI. The server features 32 GB of system memory, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio (8.0 GB per vCPU), paired directly with 960 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and 1 complimentary public IPv4 address. No discrete GPU hardware is present.

Benchmark results demonstrate mixed performance characteristics defined by its core density. Single-threaded synthetic compute exhibits strong output, placing in the top 10% on stress-ng single-core tests (3,432.18) and showing strong results for single-threaded gzip compression (32.27 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (14.68 GB/sec). Large block memory write bandwidth ranks in the top 25% at 122.3 GB/sec, matching a strong PassMark memory rating of 2,805.81. Conversely, the 4-vCPU ceiling constrains multi-threaded scaling. Multi-core stress-ng (13,688.67), Geekbench multi-core (5,944.0), and PassMark CPU score (11,756.43) sit in the average bracket, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression falls into the bottom 25% (29.25 GB/sec).

Throughput benchmarks highlight clear execution boundaries. In-memory Redis performance reaches an average 10.91 million SET operations per second, whereas PassMark database operations (2,264.13) and static web serving throughput (3.86 GB/sec) test in the bottom 25%. LLM inference demonstrates usable throughput on lightweight models, achieving 583.18 prompt tokens per second and 159.19 generation tokens per second on a 135M model, but drops sharply on a 7B model to 12.73 prompt tokens per second and 8.76 generation tokens per second due to the lack of dedicated acceleration.

Given its high memory allocation per vCPU and substantial 960 GB local NVMe storage, this configuration is cost-efficient for memory-sensitive services that require dedicated CPU time without needing high multi-core concurrency. It serves effectively for caching layers, intermediate ETL pipelines, software compilation environments, and memory-bound background tasks, while being less suited for high-concurrency web tiers or demanding AI model serving.
